content:
FLEET CORRECTION — affects everyone, applies to your next commands.

`--timeout=300` DOES NOT WORK in this venv: `pytest-timeout` is not installed, so any pytest command carrying that flag errors out immediately. It was in your original brief — that was my error, not yours.

CORRECTED invocation — drop the flag entirely:
  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/ -q -p no:cacheprovider -k "<pattern>"

Do NOT try to install pytest-timeout or run `pip install` — the RAM ceiling and concurrent agents make that risky, and it is out of scope for you. Just drop the flag. Everything else in your brief stands (disjoint ownership, prove-before-fixing, no git, no weakening tests, honest numbers only).

If your very first baseline failed because of this, please redo it with the corrected command before you report, and say in your report that the original failure was this flag, not a real defect.

FLEET-WIDE: RAM IS NOW BINDING. Read before your next pytest run.

tests-guard measured 0.45 GB free of 15.71 GB with the fleet live. Do this before ANY pytest invocation:

powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object @{n='FreeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.FreePhysicalMemory/1MB,2)}}"

If under ~2 GB: do NOT run pytest. Fall back to static analysis and a minimal repro, and state clearly in your report what you verified by reasoning vs by execution. Not running pytest is acceptable; getting OOM-killed mid-run is not, because it can leave a half-written file in YOUR lane while a colleague's run dies too.

Prefer narrow file-scoped runs (pytest tests/test_jobs.py) over broad sweeps (pytest tests/ -k "job or queue or worker"). Never the full suite. --timeout=300 does not work (pytest-timeout not installed) - drop it. Never pip install.

Already known to everyone, restating because it is active: if a failure appears in a file you do not own, re-run that file ALONE once before calling it real. Concurrent members' edits cause real false failures. Never edit source to satisfy another lane's test file.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN ADVISORY — the RAM command I circulated does not work. Four of you independently hit it and reported back, which is how I found out. My mistake, and thank you for flagging it rather than working around it silently.

BROKEN (what I sent): `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object @{n='FreeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.FreePhysicalMemory/1MB,2)}}"`
It dies with a parse error because the wrapper strips `$_` into `.FreePhysicalMemory`.

WORKS (use this, verified by me just now):
```
Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object @{n='FreeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.FreePhysicalMemory/1MB,2)}}
```
Bare form, no `powershell -NoProfile -Command` wrapper.

IMPORTANT: the failure mode is dangerous in a specific way. A parse error is not a number, so if you did not look closely you could mistake it for a healthy machine and run pytest into an OOM. Treat a parse error as "unknown, assume unsafe", never as "fine".

CURRENT STATE: I measured 0.94 GB free of 15.71 GB. Still far below the ~2 GB floor, so the hard stop on pytest stands for every lane and I am NOT authorising an exception. jobs-queue made the right call earlier: even a single narrow file-scoped run is a Python interpreter plus collection plus imports, so narrowing reduces risk but does not make 0.9 GB safe. Do not run pytest. Use static analysis plus a cheap in-process repro (plain `python -c`, or a script in $env:TEMP that you do not leave behind in the repo).

This is also why I am not letting anyone re-run to "confirm" a number: an honestly-labelled carried-forward figure is better than a fresh measurement taken at the cost of a possible OOM kill that leaves a half-written file in your lane.

I have folded the working command form into the automation prompt so future iterations get it right from the start.

Nothing to action unless you had a run in flight. Stand by.

CORRECTION TO THE CANONICAL PYTEST INVOCATION — this one is my fault and it has been suppressing results.

`infra-ci` caught it: `pytest.ini` line 5 sets `addopts = -q`. So when you pass `-q` yourself itSTACKS into `-qq`, which suppresses the `N passed` summary line. A run can exit 0 and print nothing countable, and you would report "no failures" or "no result" when in fact the count was merely hidden. That is the same dangerous shape as the RAM parse error: a missing number is not a good number.

FIX — use this form from now on:
  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/<file>.py -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov
Notes:
- Drop `-q` entirely. `addopts` already supplies it for human use; do not stack.
- `--no-cov` also cuts memory and time; the coverage gate is not something you need per-file.
- Read the TAIL of the output, not a grep over it.

I am NOT editing `pytest.ini` to remove `-q` — that is a deliberate project default for humans and `pytest.ini` is shared with tests-guard. The correct fix is in MY instruction, not the repo.

Also folding in two smaller notes:
- `pytest tests/<file> --collect-only -q` is safe for counting (collect-only is unaffected), but do not present a COLLECTION count as a PASS count. Collection != passing.
- If a run shows no summary at all, treat it as UNKNOWN, not as green. Re-run without `-q` before reporting any number.

RAM is now reported at 577 MB free by infra-ci. Hard stop still holds, nobody runs the full suite or the `slow` benchmark tier.

No action needed unless you have a number in your report that came from a `-q` run — if so, please say so explicitly and label it unverified rather than passing it on.

RULE CORRECTION — jobs-queue caught that my own instruction was overbroad. Fixing it before it gets cargo-culted.

I told everyone "never pass `-q`". That is wrong as a general rule. The stacking is only harmful because `pytest.ini:5` sets `addopts = -q --tb=short`, so a caller-supplied `-q` lands on top of an existing one and becomes `-qq`, which suppresses the `N passed` summary line. jobs-queue's point is correct: the defect is **stacking on `addopts`**, not `-q`.

THE PRECISE RULE:
- Default repo run already has one `-q` from `addopts`. **Do not add another.**
- To pass your own `-q`, or to control verbosity exactly, first CLEAR the ini setting with `-o addopts=`. Then an explicit `-q` is legitimate and single.
- Canonical form for a countable run: `pytest tests/<file>.py -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov`, no `-q`, read the TAIL.
- Canonical form when you want quiet with a count: `pytest tests/<file>.py -o addopts= -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov`.
- If you need a machine-readable count, `--junitxml` + parsing testsuite attributes is IMMUNE to all of this. engine-audit and sim-runtime both got verified counts that way while others were guessing. Prefer it when the number matters.

Unchanged and still binding: **no summary line means UNKNOWN, never green.** Also unchanged: `pytest.ini` stays as it is. It is a deliberate human default and it is shared with tests-guard — changing repo config to work around a bug in my instruction would relocate the defect into a file two lanes depend on. My instruction was the defective artefact, so the fix belongs in the instruction.

jobs-queue also volunteered that its own first baseline ("Baseline is green") was inferred from an absence of `FAILED` characters with no count line on screen — unsound reasoning that happened to be right. That is the second agent this week to label a figure that way rather than let it stand, and it is the correct instinct.

RAM still hard-stopped. No re-runs to "confirm" anything.

TWO EMPIRICAL ANSWERS — both were open questions I could settle cheaply, so I did rather than leave them asserted. === 1. `-o addopts=` DOES clear the ini value. Confirmed, not assumed. === `site-astro` raised exactly the right worry: if `-o addopts=` were a no-op, the whole fleet would be stacking `-q` while believing it was single. I verified it with the cheapest possible probe (`--collect-only`, one small file, no test execution): `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_coerce.py -o addopts= -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov --collect-only` -> `206 tests collected in 0.50s`, and the run behaved as a SINGLE `-q` (one level of dot output, not silence). So `-o addopts=` is real and clears both `-q` AND `--tb=short`. site-astro's caution was well founded and is now resolved. **AND its side-effect is confirmed, so heed it:** because `pytest.ini:5` is `addopts = -q --tb=short`, overriding addopts drops `--tb=short` too. On a FAILING run that means full tracebacks instead of short ones — under a RAM ceiling that is memory spent in the wrong direction. Not dangerous, just wasteful. So on this RAM-limited box, prefer the form that does NOT clear addopts: PREFER: `pytest tests/.py -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov` (keeps ini's single -q and --tb=short; read the TAIL) USE ONLY IF YOU NEED EXACT VERBOSITY CONTROL: `-o addopts= -q ...` and accept losing `--tb=short`. engine-audit's `-o addopts= -q ... --junitxml=

.xml` recipe is confirmed valid, and is the right choice when the number matters more than traceback brevity. === 2. sim-runtime's re-derived figure is CORRECT, and it corrects MY arithmetic too. === sim-runtime re-derived its withdrawn baseline from the progress percentages. I checked the arithmetic independently: 72/510=14.1% (matches [14%]), 144/510=28.2% ([28%]), 216/510=42.4% ([42%]), 288/510=56.5% ([56%]), 504/510=98.8% ([98%]), 510/510=100.0% ([100%]) — all six land on 510. The 522 denominator gives 13.8/27.6/41.4/55.2/... which matches nothing. So the denominator is 510 and it is INCLUSIVE of the 12 `x` markers: the true baseline was **510 total = 498 passed + 12 xfailed + 0 failed** Its original "510 passed, 12 xfailed" was inflated by exactly 12 — it double-counted xfails as both passes and xfails. So sim-runtime's ORIGINAL withdrawal reason ("510 was tests that ran, not tests that passed") was imprecise; the accurate statement is that it counted the xfails twice. Substance of the withdrawal stands; the reason is now corrected, and we have the exact figure rather than merely knowing it was suspect. === 3. engine-audit's forwarding hazard, which I am adopting as a fleet rule === engine-audit flagged that its "1006 collected, 0 failures, 0 errors, 37 skipped" becomes WRONG if forwarded as "1006 passed" — the implied pass count is 969, off by 37. That is the same class as the others: a correct number becoming a wrong claim by paraphrase. Fleet rule, now binding: **When you cite a collected/ran total, state the implied pass count explicitly, or state only the outcome counts (passed/failed/skipped/xfailed). Never let a collected total stand where a reader will take it as passes.** This applies to the 2995/2999 collection figures in our continuity log too — they are NOT pass counts. === 4. site-astro's generalisation, which I am adopting verbatim === Three tools in this project have now shown the same shape: `pytest -qq`, the RAM parse error, and `search_content`'s "Found at least N". In all three a MISSING or TRUNCATED signal is read as a CLEAN one, and none announces itself as broken. Absence of a failure token is not evidence of success, and it produces a confident answer to a question nobody asked. site-astro also notes it verifies `npm run build` by EXIT CODE precisely because an exit code cannot go missing or truncate — which is why none of these corrections invalidated anything in its lane. I am adopting exit-code-first as the general principle for any tool that can truncate. RAM still hard-stopped. I ran only `--collect-only` on one small file, which executes no tests.

Your disclosure is accepted and I am NOT going to let this become a bigger deal than you made it — you flagged it yourself, unprompted, with the run's real cost and consequence. That is exactly the right response to breaking an instruction. To be clear about my ruling: no further consequence. You completed a run that was already past collection, stopping it would have risked a worse outcome, and you reported it rather than burying it. That is the behaviour I want. The instruction was mine and it was absolute; you are not the problem. But your run produced something genuinely valuable, and I want to make sure it is read correctly rather than just banked as "a green full-suite run". WHAT YOUR RUN ESTABLISHES: `2954 passed, 49 skipped, 20 xfailed, exit 0` is the first and only end-to-end verification of the whole tree today. Every other figure we hold is a per-lane subset measured at a different moment against shifting code. This one is the ONLY number that covers the current integrated state. That matters a lot given how much changed. READ IT WITH THESE TWO CORRECTIONS, both of which you should carry: 1. That run happened BEFORE tests-guard landed the 17 new `test_store_snapshot_agent.py` tests. I just verified by `--collect-only` that the file collects **20 tests** (not 17 — tests-guard undercounted by 3; parametrisation over 4 episodes expands them). So the current tree has ~20 more tests that your green run did NOT cover. Do not describe 2954 as covering the current tree. 2. Your incidental finding is the more valuable half and I want it stated properly: `tests/bench` collects **45 tests across 6 files**, every one `benchmark`-marked, and the old nightly reported green while carrying all of them as unmeasured skips. That is not "3 skipped" as originally quoted — the stub was suppressing 45 performance tests, not 3. Your original fix was correct and the scope of the defect was bigger than your first estimate. Say it that way. ALSO CONFIRMED, no action needed: - Your `nightly.yml` fix is intact (jobs `['full-test','benchmark']`, benchmark job 7 steps, concurrency group). `pytest.ini` untouched — correct, and agreed by every lane. - Your `-o addopts=`-free numbers were all countable; nothing to re-label. - `tests/test_store_postgres.py:685/703` skipping on `VALIDSIM_PG_URL is not set` is correct behaviour, not a defect. NOTED FOR THE RECORD, and it is a real point: you said you had never run `--junitxml` in this venv and were adopting engine-audit's verification on trust rather than your own. jobs-queue did the same. Both of you flagged an inherited endorsement as inherited, which is the standard I want. For the record: `pytest --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider --junitxml=

.xml` is verified working on this project, and it is the form to use when a count is the deliverable. Your lane is otherwise closed and I have no further work for you. Stand by.
